utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue with the examination-in-chief of Mr. Zivanovic, I'd like to inform the parties that the Chamber will -- for very practical reasons has to cancel its intention to have a housekeeping session on the 25th of October. So therefore we'll not be sitting on that day. It was too difficult to get all the teams together. And another -- the Chamber was informed that the order of cross-examining the present witness was changed slightly. The Chamber was glad to hear that the Defence teams agreed for another sequence, because the Chamber had some concerns that always when we're running out of time it's usually the last Defence counsel that is -- is the target to say, and the Chamber, even if we would not have been informed about this, it was on our list to invite the parties to always consider what would be the best sequence, not to make one of you the standard victim of -- of a lack of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We do. And I decided to take on that role today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- yes. So that really was -- I expressed this not just on the basis of -- of our information but also as a genuine concern of the Chamber wanting to give all parties equal opportunities, all Defence parties as well. Then I -- finally, there's one matter, very brief matter. The newest amendment to the indictment, I think that we asked the parties not only to express their views on whether there were any objections against naming one of these witnesses but also whether there would be any problem in adding some of the persons mentioned earlier to the list of witnesses. I think that we did not receive any answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer is that the Trial Chamber, as far as we're concerned, will have an answer in writing before tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, in other words, by the time the Trial Chamber is at its desk tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll read that response. Then, Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has filed the fourth amended indictment this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Along with the new -- the proposed addition of the three witnesses and 92 bis applications for all three of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we had invited the Defence to already express their views on an additions to the witness list right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because that's what was already announced in order to speed up matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a matter, essentially, of the form in which the evidence is proposed to be adduced that may require a short submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So not adding to the list but rather the way in which -- Okay. Then, Mr. Zivanovic, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Then, Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before going on with the questions I was asking you yesterday evening, I want to go back to one issue that we discussed a little earlier in your testimony. And for those following the transcript, I'm referring to pages 9425 and 6. And could you turn, please, to tab 19 in the bundle, please. Tab 19 is annex 40 for this witness's 92 ter statement and marked as P1055. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I asked you yesterday some questions about item number 5 on that order dated the 1st of June, and in particular, the deployment of a tank platoon of the 125th Motorised Brigade BG-3 to provide assistance to MUP forces along the Crnobreg-Prejlep road. Yesterday in relation to that, first of all, I asked you to confirm that that was an order that predated the authorisation to engage the VJ in anti-terrorist operations and you confirmed that that was correct. And then I asked you, and you confirmed, that the role of the tank platoon in that operation was purely for psychological support. And I asked you whether that was in fact the way in which it had been used, and you said, "I think that did actually happen. The tank did not fire a single projectile." I wonder in that context if I could just ask you, please, to turn not in that bundle but perhaps to the screen to annex 41 to your witness statement marked as P1056, which is a regular combat report signed by Colonel Lazarevic for the 3rd of June. Can you, first of all, confirm that that is a correct description of the document? Mr. Zivanovic, I'm just --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document dated the 3rd of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it is a -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph are you referring me to?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I -- can I ask you, please, to turn to paragraph 3, which, if you could pick it up, please, on the third line down in paragraph 3, which is, again, the fourth line down, in fact, in -- in the English translation. The English translation reads: "The tank platoon of BG-3 of the 125th Motorised Brigade coordinated with MUP units during an attack along the Crnobreg-Prilep village axis. This -- the task was completed by 1400 hours with the use of five tank projectiles."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that the same deployment as the one that we were describing -- or you were describing in the previous annex as a deployment in which the tanks did not fire a single projectile?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several orders to provide support to the MUP along the Decani-Prilep axis. This is one of the orders. What I explained was an order according to which a projectile had not been fired; whereas, according to this one, it had been fired. This is a different order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So the order we were discussing yesterday, which is behind tab 19, signed by Major General Pavkovic, and which orders the deployment of the tank platoon of the 125th Motorised Brigade BG-3 to assist MUP forces along the Crnobreg-Prilep village road, that is an order that resulted, you say, in no projectiles being fired; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what it says here, that's correct. There is no order of the 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- this is a report, though, is it not, dated the 3rd of June relating to operations that have been conducted the previous day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the previous day or on that day, because normally the information referring to a particular day are written on the eve of that same day -- on the evening of that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if you look at any other part of this document -- just cast your eye over annex 41, Mr. Zivanovic. It's referring throughout, is it not, to activities on the 2nd of June?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in item 3, it is stated "in the course of the day," and the document is dated the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I understand what your evidence is on this, then, please. Is it your testimony that -- that following the order issued on the 1st, there was a deployment that resulted in no projectiles being fired because the tanks were there purely for psychological support but then the next day there was a second operation in which five projectiles were fired on the same axis by the same tank platoon? Is that what your testimony amounts to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I would like -- this is how I would like you to understand what I'm saying, because I don't have the order of the 2nd or the 3rd of June here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just included in your question that, looking at annex 41, it's referring throughout, is it not, to activities on the 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In 2.2, I see at 11.15 hours on the 3rd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore I have some difficulties in following you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right. There -- we have references from the beginning to the end to events taking place on the 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But not exclusively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to return, please, if I may, to the position we were at yesterday afternoon. And for that purpose, could you please again remove the map that was behind tab 1C. I don't know whether it's separated in your bundle.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to recap -- just to recap, if I may, as to where we were. Behind tab 23 in the Defence green file we looked yesterday at annex 51 to your statement, which is Exhibit P1065, which is the order of the 23rd of July, deploying BG-3 along an axis from Dolac to Iglarevo to Kijevo and BG-2 to take part in a blockade of Junik. And we then looked at tab 24, annex 52 to your statement, Exhibit P1066, which is the order by yourself of the 24th of July confirming that BG-2 is in effect to close off the village of Junik and BG-3 to provide support for the PJP on the axis described from Dolac to Iglarevo to Kijevo. Now, I want, please, against that background to look with you behind tab 25. And this should not be shown on the screen. This is Exhibit D78, a situation report filed by Colonel Crosland on the 30th of July relating to a tour of duty on the 28th and 29th of July. And just in order to orientate ourselves on this map, after the summary section of this report, the first entry under the heading "Detail" reads: "Orahovac-Malisevo. Tour departed Prizren 28th of July traveling north to Zrze through MUP VCP vehicle check-point in Bijela Crkva to Orahovac." And then if I can just paraphrase the second paragraph. The tour then entered Malisevo and, picking it up just after the first full paragraph on the second page, it reads, under 2: "Tour released and allowed to proceed north towards main Pec-Pristina road. Prior to junction where six times VJ T-55 facing towards Malisevo. At Lapusnik junction one strike force of approximately 150 mixed SAJ, PJP, and VJ and APCs gathered to launch assault on Malisevo. Comment, commander of the force somewhat surprised to see tour arriving from the direction of his intended objective." Now, pausing there for a moment, we can see from this document and from the testimony that we've heard that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That the military attache's tour of duty, if we can look at it on the map, is proceeding in a north-easterly direction from Malisevo towards the Lapusnik junction. And Colonel Crosland testified that it was at that junction that he encountered Milorad Ulemek, or Milorad Lukovic, or Legija who introduced himself as being in overall command of this joint strike force, involving combined SAJ, PJP, and VJ forces. Now, can you help us, please. We know that you had deployed your forces along the main Pec road via Dolac and Iglarevo to Kijevo. Were they your forces also at the junction of Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just dropping down a little further, after the heading "Commensurate proof of VJ involvement in non-border ops," under 3, Colonel Crosland's tour then turned left, or west, on the main road. So having reached the Lapusnik junction, it reads: "Tour turned west on main road in direction of Pec and encountered further MUP elements dug in all along the road. At Kijevo a second strike group of approximately 300 mixed JSO with APCs, VJ with M80s, MT55 Bridgelayer, and MUP in six cargo lorries, ready to move in the direction of Malisevo." Now, pausing there. This is Kijevo he's describing. Presumably they would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Presumably they would be the forces of BG-3 that you yourself had deployed along the access from Dolac via Iglarevo to Kijevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, if we're referring to the 28th and the 29th of July, for this reason: From the moment the order was issued, Combat Group 3 entered Kijevo, spent the night there, and went back. The rest was done by the MUP forces and my neighbour, who was there along that axis. I believe you mentioned Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So your forces went as far as Kijevo, spent the night there, is that correct, and then came back the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They joined up with the MUP forces that had been deployed in Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And would that have been the 25th to the 26th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the report before me. If I issued an order on the 25th, then it must have been on the 26th and the 27th, if I'm not mistaken. Please allow me to look at the date of the order. The date of the order is the 24th. Then it must have been the 25th and the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we just look at the comments immediately following that, having encountered this mixed force at Kijevo, you can see Colonel Crosland's tour, it says, "continued west along the main road, which was again held by a mixed force of VJ/MUP up to the Grebnik vehicle check-point." And if we look on the map, Grebnik is immediately south of Dolac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just so that we're clear, having encountered the joint force at Lapusnik under Milorad Ulemek, the village military attache then encounters a joint force at Kijevo and continues west towards Pec as far as Dolac and Grebnik. And if you just look at the document and the comment that follows: "Every village from Lapusnik westwards have suffered deliberate damage by cannon and heavy mortar gun fire. Many houses burning. Garages and businesses trashed." Now, the damage he's describing is along the axis that your men had been ordered by you to travel 24 hours previously; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part the territory covered by my neighbour at Lapusnik from Kijevo to Iglarevo was covered by that. This was a great difficulty for our unit to go through that area, as we were providing support to the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- the point is simply this: On the 24th, you order BG-3 along this axis as far as Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say they went there on the 24th and came back on the 26th. And here, apparently, on the 28th the British military attache's tour retraces your steps and on every village west of Lapusnik on the main road as far as Dolac he encounters deliberate damage, houses burning and garages and businesses trashed. Now, presumably you're going to tell us your men were not involved in that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. My men were involved in that on the 25th and the 26th. I said that they spent the night at Kijevo and withdrew toward Grebnik. They fired upon what was considered to be military targets out of which fire had been opened upon the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that would have included garages and businesses along the way.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state exactly whether every garage held a sniper shooter or a sharp shooter, and my forces had the orders to fire wherever a terrorist was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just drop town to 5, to the other part of the operation that you authorised on the 24th in relation to the blockade of Junik. You can see the entry there: "Junik area. Tour heard and observed the fall of shot into Junik throughout the afternoon of the 28th of July. From line of sight approximately 4 kilometres distant. Also heard MBT and APC heavy mortar gun/cannon fire together with mortars."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Is that my order you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm reading from the report of the British military attache at item 5. Let me just fill it in for you a little bit by reference to the testimony, which is, for the record, transcript 3084 to 3097. The testimony that the Trial Chamber has heard in relation to this entry is that the military attache was in a position to observe four hours of direct and indirect fire on the village of Junik as well as the villages of Prejlep, Irzniq, and Gllogjan from the south end of the lake. Now, pausing there. Your order of the 24th of July had been part, had it not, of the coordinated action with the PJP to blockade Junik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only a part of my forces, Combat Group 2, and elements of Combat Group 3. In the encirclement or the blockade that there were more forces of the MUP and the VJ that were not under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you aware that that operation was to be coordinated with heavy shelling from the south end of the lake to the village of Junik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that this was supposed to be done that way. You know how far the lake was from my positions, and I had no way of influencing the forces over there by the lake. The MUP forces entered Junik, if I'm not mistaken, on the 15th and the 16th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm speaking at the moment not about the entry on the 15th and 16th of August but about an afternoon of continuous shelling for four hours from a long range from the southern tip of Lake Radoniq. And what I'm trying to understand is that we can see from your order of the 24th that, just to use your words, the task you authorised BG-3 to do, together with BG-2 or a part of BG-2 and the PJP, was to close off the village of Junik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And the exact line was mentioned. That was the village of Miroc [phoen], a Muslim cemetery, and I believe it was trig point 505.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I -- you can see in this order here under 5, security measures, fire is to be opened only upon fortified features out of which terrorist forces are active. I tried to prevent any sort of abuse, especially in regard to Junik, because before the date ordered, the 15th or the 16th, we had not been allowed by anyone to enter the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you knew there were civilians in Junik and a significant civilian population there at the end of July, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's debatable whether there were civilians or not. My scouts reported to me that there were no civilians; rather, that there were some 300 to 400 terrorists, also in the direction of the village of Jasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so are we to understand the position that when you deployed your forces of BG-2 and BG-3 to assist in the blockade of Junik, you did not know that there were plans to mount a shelling operation two days later on the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did order and I stand by that that my units were in the deblocking, but the units you mentioned down by the Radonjic Lake were not my units. I wasn't informed about heavy Howitzer fire and their engagement. There was fire upon a feature above Jasic. I am aware of that. But I wasn't aware of Junik. At the time, I was in Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, now to tab 2 in the bundle, which I -- I think is your report of this collection of operations that had taken place between the 25th of July and the 7th of August. This is D165 and annex 56 to your statement. And whilst we're doing that, Your Honour, I should note that the map that we've used with this witness, which differs to some extent from that which is in the e-court system, has been uploaded in its form as used with the witness with Defence identification 1D64-0024 and I believe provisionally allocated the exhibit number D181 and may I ask that it be marked for identification under that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's correct. It will be marked for identification as D181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just look briefly at this order, please -- I'm sorry, this report. First of all, can you confirm, Mr. Zivanovic, this is you reporting on the 8th of August on the deployments that have taken place between the 25th of July and the 7th of August? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we can see, if we look under item number 1 -- if I've understood this correctly. This is you describing the deployment of Combat Group 3 on the 25th and 26th of July along the access that -- the axis that we have examined from Dolac via Iglarevo to Kijevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You then indicate that on the 2nd to the 6th of August, the 3rd PJP Detachment with support from BG-1 was deployed on the Novo Selo-Krusevac-Morina village to Rezala village axis. Is that part of the same operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was an operation in the municipality of Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just pick on just one or two of the bullet points here and ask for your help with those, please. If we look at, I think, bullet point number 6 under 1, it indicates that on the 5th of August the Brazil Group and the 4th PGP -- PJP Detachment with support from BG-3 were deployed on the Malizgan to Ovcarevo axis. Can you just summarise in a sentence or two what that deployment involved, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, this is the axis from Klina to Srbica -- or rather, that road there. And we supported the groups mentioned -- the units mentioned here, the 4th Detachment and the Brazil Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did your troops enter Ovcarevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not given the tasks to enter there but to stop at the edge; whereas, for the entry into village, that was primarily the task of -- because what this refers to is a tank and a tank can easily be set on fire in a village. It's quite vulnerable in inhabited areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the ground troops that went in were the Brazil Group and the PJP; is that right? To Ovcarevo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, presumably, because there was no one else who could have entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This was roughly a week, was it, after the fall of Malisevo, after Serb forces had taken control of Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. When was it? On the 28th or the 29th. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In that region, certainly. It was either the 28th or the 29th. I wonder if we could just play a short passage of video at this point. And it will be the piece of film for which the transcript is behind tab 30G. This piece of film shows a Serbian military operation in Ovcarevo approximately a week after the fall of Malisevo, according to the commentary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The transcript has been given to the booth, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The transcript is behind tab 30G in the bundle, which the booth have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the same instructions, as always, as far as the booth is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: The Serbs know that they have the rebel ethnic Albanians on the run and again today they have been pushing the advantage. This is Ovcarevo village, the latest Kosovo Liberation Army position to fall to the Serb offensive, the latest place to be emptied of its civilian population. The United States special envoy to the region toured Central Kosovo today. He saw it firsthand, some of the destruction. "We've condemned it very much and it's simply intolerable to see these growing number of refugees. And as you may have heard, there are apparently an additional 30.000 or so in the late few days who have gone north." The aid effort is beginning to gain pace. One of the first convoys passed through Malisevo. It fell to the Serbs a week ago and since then the town is burned. In the hills the village of Loxhejve serves as a refugee centre. The supplies will be stored here and then distributed to the people. But there are those who have not been reached by the aid efforts. In these woods, we found as many as a thousand refugees. The families try to cope but mostly they sit and wait for news. They don't know it yet, but many of their homes have been destroyed and there is nothing to go back to. She is less than a week old, born as a refugee in a field. Tonight she and everyone else here will once again sleep outside. The forecast is for rain. The people here say they would like to go home, but while the fighting continues, they say they have no choice but to stay here in the woods with no shelter and very little food or water. Jeremy Cooke, BBC News, Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, pausing there, Mr. Zivanovic, the forces that we saw in the first part of that film, which according to the commentary were in Ovcarevo, are you able to recognise those forces according to their appearance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Must I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can answer the question, yes, of course, you should answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have recognised. These are the PJP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, again, so that we're clear, that -- this would have been the operation that your forces were tasked to support; is that correct? In Ovcarevo a week after the fall of Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we see there in that report a reference to Malisevo being in effect on fire. Again, are you able to help us, was there a great deal of burning as far as you were aware in the area of Malisevo at this part of this operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never entered Malisevo. I haven't done that since 1979 or 1980. I apologise, but that's outside of my area. That's why I cannot answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in combat operations anywhere else. If fire was opened from a building, then yes, the fire was returned and that building was treated as a military target. I expect that it was destroyed or burned as a result of that. As for sweeping and verifying, then yes, we normally check the area for terrorists, and there are rules as to how a building is checked for that. Three to five people are assigned to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just turning back for a moment to tab 25. That is D78, and to the observations of the British military attache on the 29th of July. On page 3 under "Bravo," it reads as follows: "Wanton damage. Every village adjacent to both avenues into Malisevo had suffered severe damage. Houses still burning. Businesses and garages deliberately vandalised. Crops, both corn and maize and vineyards burnt. Some animals killed." And did you receive reports that vineyards were being put to the torch in this way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. This is the first time I hear that any vineyard was torched. This is the first I hear of it, now in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if we go back then, please, to your report of the 8th of August, behind tab 2. This is the report in which you indicate that on -- as far as I can understand it, all of the axes apart from those that are listed in 1.2 in the first three bullet points, on all of the remaining axes the Brazil Group carried out deep wedging and burning operations that you described to us in your testimony last week and in the diagram that you drew. Now, have I understood your testimony correctly that -- that "wedging" is a technical military term but "burning" is not? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't use it. As for this particular operation, I watched when the SAJ at a feature near Rezalo was present. There was a hill there that could not be taken. That's what I have to say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I'm trying to understand is if the word "burning" has no specific military connotation as a term of art, how it would be understood by the people reading this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that they cover every decimetre of soil with ammunition, with missiles, in 10 to 15 metres of any area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, my -- my question is rather a narrower one than that. If "burning" is not a military term of art, it's not a technical term used in the military, I wondered how it would be that other people would understand what you meant by it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my superior understood me. That meant the use of all resources at his disposal so that this strip of 10 to 15 metres was safe enough, neutralised, for an infantry person or somebody on foot to go by. This does not refer to any inhabited areas. This doesn't refer to burning, use of napalm, or any other incendiary means. No, this just refers or means the use of ammunition, firearms ammunition, artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm interested as well in the date of -- of -- of this document. We see that it refers at the top, reference your order, strictly confidential, number 880/175 of the 7th of August. Do you see that at the top?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see this. This is an order of my superior command, which tasked me with sending such a report. The reason for sending this report, I actually don't know why the commander -- or what the commander wanted by way of this report. I can only assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am only asking because you'll remember that yesterday behind tab 28 - don't bother to turn it up - we looked at an extract from the minutes of the Joint Command for Kosovo dated the 7th of August in which Mr. Sainovic had recorded concern that great damage was being caused to Serbia by unnecessary burning of houses. And I just wondered whether the request that you were receiving on that day for a report was in any way connected to concern being expressed about the wanton damage that was being inflicted.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw yesterday for the first time the page of the minutes. That's the first thing. The second thing, I can only make assumptions as to why the commander asked for that. We complained, we, the army, saying that they asked for us to provide support but they were not skilled enough when it came to supporting our combat vehicles. They would leave our tanks without support. For example, a tank, 72, normally has a three- or four-member crew, and they would leave them at the mercy of the enemy. This is why we asked that they be more careful in providing support to our technical equipment and crews. And this is why there was some friction between us and MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look at paragraph 1.4 in this report, please, where -- where the engagement of combat equipment during this phase of the operation is recorded. And it -- the indication is that BGs 1, 3, and 4 used T-55 tanks and 122-millimetre Howitzers. And then it says: "The only prohibited equipment used were the 122-millimetre Howitzers, with one platoon giving supporting fire to the Brazil Group and another to the 3rd PJP Detachment." First of all, can you just help us. Why were those weapons prohibited, in your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in early August an order arrived from the commander of the army where he banned the use of Howitzers without his prior consent. This here pertains to a peak near the village of Rezalo when the Brazil Group was making a breakthrough, they needed support from the territory in-depth, which is according to our artillery rules. And this is why the commander issued this order and fired one missile and then he was criticised for doing that without calling me or the army commander prior to doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In general terms, Mr. Zivanovic, you had for the purposes of these operations, I think, authorised 120-millimetre mortar platoon to be available for the engagements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A platoon of Howitzers, 122-millimetre, is a component of BG-1, a battery that has six pieces. So it was an integral part of the equipment of BG-1. Wherever BG-1 went, this Howitzer followed. And it wasn't me who approved it. I said that the commander on his own decided to open fire, and this is why he was called to explain it later on. He was criticised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. No, I -- I'm sorry, my question was slightly different. In the order that you issued on the 24th of July, behind tab 24, you personally authorised a 120-millimetre mortar platoon to be ready to support forces both defending the barracks and in isolated installations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. A platoon of mortar -- mortars of 120 millimetres, yes. That's an infantry piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you're going through quite a lot of details here, where we're limited in time, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And I will speed up, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the level of details is not always necessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And paragraph 2 in this document is a report on whether there had been excesses in the use of force by units and MUP forces on the axes. And you record that according to your observations there was no excessive use of force but when combat operations were being conducted, due to the high temperature resistance offered from certain houses and the use of tracer ammunitions, haystacks, wheat, and wooden ancillary buildings caught fire. That is a report back -- were you specifically being requested to report back on excesses, or was that part of a standard report?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is this MFI P1066? Can I just ask that the exhibit number be put on the record so we don't lose it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where -- what I'm asking about now is tab 2, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's P --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's D165. It is annex 56 to this witness's witness statements. It's a previously exhibited document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the question, Mr. Zivanovic, was: Was that a specific request for you to provide a report back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this particular case, I was asked to report on this. And I apologise. I misunderstood something that you said. It wasn't that the houses opened fire. The houses cannot do that. It's the terrorists who open fire from buildings, houses, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, just to help us with one matter. Could you look at the photographs, please, behind tab 31. And I make it clear these are undated. Could you just help us, please, from the uniforms as to who it is or which contingent it is that appear in that group of photographs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are members of the army. I'm looking at the person who stands on the left. The first on the left, he has trousers which are atypical for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see any army insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If you would just like to look very briefly at 31C, you will see that the character on the far left has his shoulder turned towards the camera and there is an insignia on his right shoulder, which you will see blown up behind tab 31D. Does that assist you at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could it be blown up, please, so that I can see the emblem. We did not have such berets. We do not have them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not have the black hats.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you bear with me for a moment. If you look behind tab 31C, which is not, I think, where you're looking at the moment. 31C. Yes. If you look at the gentleman on the left there. No, you're looking at --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see here that there is an emblem; but I can't tell which one. I apologise, but it's not clear, so I cannot vouch for my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, please, to turn one photograph back in your bundle. No, one photograph towards the front. Can you just go to the next photograph towards the front. Yes, that's the one. Could you just look at that photograph. And at the gentleman on the far left, can you see a patch on his shoulder?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it a bit better, but this is not a military insignia, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, Colonel Crosland testified before the Tribunal that he had a meeting with General Ojdanic at the end of the summer in which the general agreed in terms that the operations that had taken place across the summer of 1998, specifically the operations by your forces and the forces under the command of General Delic, had been grossly disproportionate. This is transcript 3063. Were you aware that General Ojdanic was expressing the view that your forces had acted in a grossly disproportionate manner?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that, and I doubt that he could have said so, when in mid-1998 there were 25.000 armed members of sabotage and terrorist forces. That has already become a rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Final topic, if I may. You were -- gave us some evidence yesterday in relation to the two maps that you had marked showing deployments in the August and September offensives. I don't ask that they be called up, but, for the record, they're P1103 and P1104. I just wanted to make sure -- whether I had understood your testimony correctly. In relation to that part of the deployments that involved Prejlep and Rznic on each occasion. First of all, in August we can see from the way that you have marked the map that -- that -- this is 1103 -- that forces under your command were stationed on the main road immediately opposite Prejlep. Could I understand the position. Did your forces enter Prejlep and Rznic in the August offensive or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- the first operation. And if I'm not mistaken, BG-3 supported it. I could be wrong, because I don't have the map in front of me. It's a tank unit. It did not enter Prilep until MUP passed Prilep. Only later a column of three tanks passed through. They walked on the left side looking from Rznic. The feature is called Grdaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not enter Rznic either. They halted outside waiting for the MUP forces to check what the situation was in Rznic. On the left side a part of their neighbour on the left entered. And if I am not mistaken, that's 15/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your statement - and I don't call it up - but at paragraph 104, when describing this operation, you indicated that "as a result" -- and I'm quoting: "As a result of using armour-piercing incendiary equipment, hand-held rocket launchers and hand grenades, around 10 houses were set on fire." Were those pieces of equipment used by your forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my units used tank rounds, and inside of Prilep there were 60 terrorists. If each building harboured three of them, that meant that there were 20 buildings there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, so far as the September offensive is concerned, at 1104 - that is the map you've marked at P1104 - we have heard evidence from Colonel Crosland who passed through, first of all, Prejlep and then Rznic on the 8th -- I'm sorry, the 9th of September indicating -- he -- the testimony that he's given indicates that there was a joint force there, which I think you've confirmed, with both T-55 - presumably battle tanks - and Praga air-defence system in support. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: BG-3 did have tanks. I told you that there are seven tanks within a BG. BG-3 did not have Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So -- so is it your testimony that the Praga air-defence system was not deployed in the September offensive in the area of Prejlep and Rznic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they were deployed -- I suppose that they were used, because they were available.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because their neighbour had them. So I suppose that they were used. And MUP also had some.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. As far as you understood the position, was it permissible for you to use anti-aircraft equipment such as the Praga for personnel use, for anti-personnel use?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combat rule for that piece of equipment envisages also targeting ground targets, fortified buildings and personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland testified that when he passed through Prejlep and Rznic on this occasion there was no sign of the presence of KLA, no return fire, but 300 combined troops, including VJ, firing indiscriminately into buildings, looting, burning animal fodder, and slaughtering livestock before the eyes of the international observers who passed by. Just to be clear, that would have been a force that included soldiers that you had deployed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question without knowing the exact position of Colonel Crosland. I was, together with the commander of BG-3, in August and no such thing happened. In September, on the other side, opposite from where BG-3 passed, I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just ask for the transcript reference of that. I was looking for it in the transcript. That is, Crosland's evidence on that exact point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's 26 -- sorry, 2969 to 2971 and 4668 to 4670. And the relevant sitrep is behind tab 26. And, for the record, is 65 ter number 1292.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in answer to your question, Mr. Zivanovic, for the purposes of clarification, the description was given in respect of an operation being conducted in Prejlep and in Rznic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which day?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the 9th of September. I'm sorry -- yes, on the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that with certainty either. BG-2, which was supposed to coordinate with them to the right of Glamoc had reached Rznic. I -- if I'm not mistaken, I don't have the map there but I remember an arrow. And I cannot guarantee you that there were no terrorist forces in that sector. Every commander is responsible for the acts of his forces in any operation of MUP and army combined, and I have to tell you that we invested great efforts in order to prevent any misconduct, abuse, and other things that I spoke of.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may also make reference to a transcript page. That's 9440, line -- no, 9439, line 25. It reads: "I will certainly conclude cross-examination within the hour."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And -- and I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- then we'll have a break, since the hour is gone by now. We'll have a break until ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- I should simply mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I should simply mention that the transcript behind tab 30G of the second videotape most recently played to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- needs to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be marked for identification as D182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll later come to what exactly is tendered and what exactly will be admitted. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I represent Lahi Brahimaj, and I want to ask you about two occasions when the forces under your command gave assistance to the MUP in attacking Jabllanice. That would be at the beginning of August and the first week of September of 1998. You understand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. The axis was, if I'm not mistaken, along the -- or in the direction of the village of Jablanica, but those were not my forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Those were the forces of the 15th Armoured Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I don't have the map here, so you'll excuse me if I have to think about it for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Let's see what -- let's see what we can do with the assistance of the documents. When -- if we could go briefly, please, to Exhibit D80. That's your tab 53. That's the decision by Commander Colonel General Pavkovic to, in his words, crush the terrorist forces centres in Likovac, Ovcarevo, and Jabllanice, and Gllogjan villages and Smonica village by of mounting synchronised operations in the Drenica and Jablanica areas and continuing the blockade of Junik and Jasic villages. Do you have the document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This is described in the first full paragraph as the -- a decision to launch the third stage of the plan. What were the first two stages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to set a time frame on that, but this is how it went roughly: The first stage was lifting the blockade of Kijevo. The second stage was, I believe, Malisevo. And this was the third stage. I have to express my reservations in telling you this, because I don't feel that I have the competence over the matter to be able to tell you about these stages. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this was Colonel General Pavkovic's request for approval to launch this third stage, as it says in that document, and it's followed in the next one by P1067 at tab 54, the same date, the 1st of August, by the same General Pavkovic's decision. Does that document have a military name? Is it a -- an -- a command order? How would you describe that document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a commander's document which states quite clearly the decision to break up and destroy. You can see that right below the heading where it says "the Command of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Now, that in itself is a fairly short document by comparison with the one I'm going to ask you to look at next, which is behind -- which is tab 82, P1092, which deals with the September operation; those two first documents dealing with the August operation. Do you have your tab 82?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This is a -- a 17-page document setting out in detail which units are to do what, what -- what preparatory steps are to be taken, et cetera, et cetera. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I believe that I made a sketch of that on the map yesterday or the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. My question is this: Would it be reasonable to assume that there must have been a similarly detailed command for the August operation, as we see here at tab 82 for the September operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying. You're saying "command." You mean the command of the Pristina Corps? Well, it had always existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, the document number 82, it's a very detailed document. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The document at 54 is just one and a half or two pages. It's a much less-detailed document. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. It can be understood as a preparatory order. It -- or it was taken out of the original document. I only have one page of it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. Now, who was responsible for selecting all of the -- the documents attached to your 92 ter statement, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that there must have been a much more detailed document than that preparatory order, as I think you just described it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer this way: It would be desirable for a clearer and more precise document to exist, although it can be issued on a page a -- or a page and a half, because the situation in Smonica had been general knowledge to us ever since the month of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we moving in circles? I do understand that you'd like to know -- at least, I would like to know on the basis of your questions by now, whether such a document exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not ask the witness. Say: Does there exist such an extensive report as well? Then we'd know and we could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You heard His Honour's question: Does there exist a more extensive order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that there never was such an order or you simply haven't located one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen one, or else I would have shown it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were asked a couple of questions by Mr. Emmerson concerning the document that you have at tab 56. That's Defence Exhibit D165. And I want you just to go back to tab 55, P1068, where General Pavkovic ordered all units to report - and I'm looking at item 2 - whether there was excessive use of force by units and MUP forces by axis. And that report is dated the 7th of August, and it relates, of course, to the operation on the 2nd and 3rd of August. Was it standard practice after every operation to request a report on whether there was excessive use of force, or was this an unusual request?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was standard practice for every commander of a combat group to make an analysis of the task implemented and to send it to the superior command according to a specific procedure. It did not have to be made, the analysis, in a couple of days' time. It could have been sent ten days later or two weeks later once all the necessary information had been gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, you do understand my question. You're an intelligent man. My question related to the use of excessive force. Was it standard to ask if there was excessive force used?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to tell you. In the analysis there is one section of the report set aside for the information concerning a possible excessive force that may have been used. So the answer was "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, the report that we have is the report from your command at tab 56, Defence Exhibit D165. We don't have a report currently before the Tribunal from the 15th Armoured Brigade. Did you not find one as you were going through exhibits with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find it because I did not want to look for documents authored by my colleagues who had their own respective tasks and obligations, if you understand what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If we could have exhibited in e-court, please, 3D01-1161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that need a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It will need a number, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be marked for identification as D183.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I regret that we do not have a copy of this document in B/S/C, so if you'll allow me, Witness, to describe it briefly to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This is the report dated the 7th of August of 1998 written by Commander Colonel Mladen Cirkovic. Is it right he was the commander of the 15th Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard the name Mladen mentioned, but it's true that it was Mladen Cirkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And this report is responding to General Pavkovic's request, just as your own report at tab 56 responded to that request. I'm going to take you down to number 2, which is, of course, responding to paragraph 2 of General Pavkovic's request about the possibility that excessive force had been used. And it reads there - and I'm reading from the English - "During operations against the armed Siptar" -- and it says here "derogatory term for Albanians" -- "separatists, not once did VJ units and MUP forces on the axes listed in item 1 use excessive force. Fire was opened on the armed Siptar separatists only to neutralise targets which were endangering human lives. The separatists opened fire from infantry weapons, 60-millimetre and 82-millimetre mortars and hand-held rocket launchers from bunkers, fortified buildings, trenches and other local features adapted for firing from. In no case was fire opened on the terrorists when it was observed that civilians, diplomatic representatives, humanitarian workers or some Monitoring Missions were in their combat deployment."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've just been handed a note, very helpfully, to say that the original of this document is at 65 ter 01290.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page, it reads at item 3: "The behaviour of the members of 15th Brigade and Combat Groups 2 and 3 of the 15th Armoured Brigade and the MUP units towards the population and their property during the operations was completely appropriate to the combat situation. We have no information regarding the behaviour of the MUP units' members after the operation, because after the end of the operations our units returned to their previous sectors." Now, were you aware of civilian casualties that were caused during that operation in Jabllanice in August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. This is the first time I hear of it. I did not proceed along that route. My colleague was in charge of that, who was under the same command as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was it part of the duty of a commander to report civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he knew, he was duty-bound to report on that. But you see that he said that he withdrew right after the action was completed, and I therefore suppose that he did not go into the inhabited area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And so the answer essentially is that if there were civilian casualties, they must have been caused by the MUP, not by the VJ.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. You'll understand that when fire is being opened from a building or from a bunker, then fire is returned. And, of course, a civilian has no business being there. The terrorist activity functioned in an interlocked way, wherever -- whenever a village was emptied of terrorists, another village would receive them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to have a look with you at your use of the word "terrorists." Now, many armies throughout history have used derogatory terms to describe their enemy, and perhaps this helps motivate troops. For instance, at tab 82, P1092, under heading 6.4 - it's the tenth page - you make a -- a major point about the importance of organising morale and psychological preparations in all units just before execution of the task to make sure that troops are motivated and ready to perform it. And you also make the point that it's important to prevent the incidence of defeatism, fear, and panic. I say "you." In fact, it's General Pavkovic. Those are important as matters of military discipline, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And is it also part of the morale and psychological preparations to use derogatory terms about the enemy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained on the first day that we referred to them as "sabotage terrorist groups," "Siptar terrorist groups," or "Siptar terrorist forces." I don't see anything derogatory in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You know, surely, don't you, that the word "Siptar" is regarded as derogatory when used by Serbs against or about ethnic Albanians in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For seven years I was in a military school. I had a room-mate, a Siptar, and he never took offence at that. He, in fact, told me himself that he was a Siptar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The expression, if we could look at P1065, which is your tab -- excuse me one second. Your tab 52. I beg your pardon. 1065 is your tab 51. You use the expression "Siptar gangs," and that is your document; correct? Under item 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you see at item 5 there that you use the term "Siptar gangs"; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the next document, at tab 52, P1066, the first paragraph, some lines down in the English: "Breaking up the Siptar hordes in the village of Junik." Again, that's your term. You habitually use this in a -- this expression as a derogatory term, did you not, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this tab, we also have the term "Siptar gangs." It's probably -- there are probably two or three documents where my operations officer used that term. When we say "gang," it's not that we want to term them in a derogatory manner. Rather, we are referring to the activities that they are conducting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Oh, it's -- it's not your document any longer now. This is your operations officer's document, is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I signed the document, which means that I stand by that document, but my operations officer drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. You never use the expression "KLA forces," or "UCK forces," do you? Not in any of your documents.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I didn't make the comparison. If I did use that term, then I probably put it in inverted commas, the "KLA."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What you do say is "the so-called KLA"; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, "the so-called KLA." I can't recognise it, since there can be only one army in a country, in one's own country.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, could you -- the Chamber considers that a lot of attention is paid to something which, unless you come to a important point soon, is -- is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm coming to it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are aware that the "so-called DDR" was an expression used by the Western Germans for 20/25 years. I think that finally that would not be the prominent aspect of the relationship between Western and Eastern Germany. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What it comes down to then, Mr. Zivanovic, is this: You did not recognise that they were really a military force. You regarded them basically as a group of gangs from different localities. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially it started out as classic terrorism known worldwide. In mid-1998 there ensued a stage that was called rebel activities. And then shortly before the NATO aggression, what followed was an armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Rather, the interpreter's correction, for the second stage not rebel activities but insurgent activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So shortly before the NATO aggression, as you call it, there was a -- an armed rebellion at that stage. So in the -- about April of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the aggressor started attacking on the 24th of March and then it continued from there onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that correction. So are we talking about January or February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about February, March, and April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's when you as a military man consider that an armed rebellion started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon. In what year are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: 1999, Your Honour. Shortly before the so-called NATO aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is that -- is that -- Mr. Zivanovic, is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. If I can add, I used the term "the so-called KLA," whereas, you use the term "the so-called NATO aggression." That's how matters stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My question, though, to you Witness - my irony aside - is: Are you saying as a military man that armed -- the armed rebellion started in approximately February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday you said "by wherever there are terrorists present, that is a target." And I -- I'd like to discuss the following with you with that in mind: As I understand your testimony, there was a offensive in August of 1998 that included, among other villages, the village of Gllogjan; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to that offensive, would it be fair to say that the following information is accurate, which is that a military convoy of approximately 110 vehicles left Peje and headed for the villages of Carrabreg, Prejlep, and Gramocelj, the villages of Baballoq, Dubrava, Lluka e Eperme, Shaptej, Gllogjan, and Izniq were targeted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct to say that the vehicles left from Pec and they took starting positions as I drew it on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would have been on the 11th of August of 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The -- the previous day, the 10th of August, attacks were launched on Gllogjan and there was fighting in Junik, Dushkaja and heavy artillery was being used for that particular assault; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which document you're referring to, especially when it comes to Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If -- I'm referring to, at this time, a report - and this is report number 430, which is in the system as 2D00-1227. And it won't be -- it won't be in the documents you have, sir. It's -- it's a report from the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms in Kosovo, in which various activities are -- are documented as just having occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could have that brought up. It's up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does it need a number, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If it could be marked for identification, I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark that for identification as D184.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm wondering if you can tell us whether the following is accurate or not, which is -- looking at page 1 of that document, and I'll read it to you because it's in English, under August 9th, referring to Decan, it says: "From 9.30 a.m. until 8.00 p.m., an attack was launched on Decan, Carrabreg i Poshtem, Prejlep, Lluka e Eperme, Rastavica, Beleg, Shaptej, Gramocelj, Junik, Gllogjan, Irzniq, and Kodrali. Now, were those -- for the 9th of August, are those all areas that were targeted in the offensive that you were engaged in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? From 9.30 in the morning until 8.00 p.m.? No way it could have lasted that long. We would have used up all the ammunition we had at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. You mentioned yesterday that in the types of weapons that you were using that you used different -- you used different kinds of ammunition and every third or fourth bullet could have been an incendiary one. Do you recall giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At PKT, every third or fifth could be that. And in PAM it's mandatory that every third one should be. That's a tactical rule on the use of that equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you by any chance help -- help me here. Do you know what a -- I think it's called a Kaqusha missile is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of Kacusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The report that I was just referring to goes on to say forwards - the same date, same page - "Different kinds of weapons were used, including 'Kaqusha' missiles." But that's something you're not familiar with. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, you mean Kaqusha. Yes, I'm aware of what that is. It's a Russian system. We have a corresponding system which is a multi-barreled rocket launcher, 128 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And all of the places that I mentioned on -- that were attacked on the 9th, those are all villages; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These settlements are villages, that's correct. About 500 terrorists were stationed there, according to -- according to our information at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On -- on August 10th - and that will be page 2 - you -- you launch an attack using both the Serbian police and military forces on Gllogjan; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On August 12th - this is page 3 - the -- the following is reported: "It is the fourth day of the Serbian offensive Defence the videolinks in the districts of Decan and Gjakova. 250 military vehicles were engaged in this action. Many villages are under attack: Junik, Gllogjan, Gramaqel, Baballoq, Shaptej, Dubrava, Lluka e Eperme, Irzniq, Prejlep, Carrabreg i Poshtem, Beleg, Kodrali, and Pozhar." Is that an accurate reflection of the villages that were under attack on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is within the spirit of the map that I drew, then yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the following occurring on the 6th of August - and that will be found at 2D1209, which is report number 429. And I'm referring the Chamber and counsel to page 2. It indicates the following report: "Last night Serbian police and military forces shelled Shaptej, Prejlep, and Carrabreg -- excuse me, Carrabreg i Poshtem. The village was shelled by" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I missed whether we are still on the same document or whether it's a new one that needs a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise. It's going to need -- it's going to need a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because if it hasn't got a number --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then Chambers have difficulties in consulting the document. Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be D185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "The village was shelled by tanks and armoured cars stationed on a hill near Prejlep and along the road from Decan to Gjakova." Are you familiar with that action being taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept everything that I drew on the map. I would like to see it, to be able to see it to verify. You are now referring to the document that I am not familiar with and I cannot follow the interpretation fast enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If -- if you had a -- a map in front of you, would that be of assistance with regard to the issue of whether or not these actions were taken on these dates?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm thinking that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the witness may be referring to Exhibit P1103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the map marked by a witness in another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's just what I was thinking, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please show that to the witness, P1103. Perhaps if you give him a hard copy. That's the -- if that would be possible, so that he could consult that, because the map -- to look at the map on the screen is not easy, because it's rather small. Mr. Emmerson, could you assist? I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have a map right there that you could give him?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have one copy of the hard copy that the witness marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could ask, first of all, to -- to ask the witness whether he could work on the basis of this. Perhaps, Madam -- well, Madam Usher has the original, I take it. Yes. Could it be shown to the witness, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take it you don't have my last question in mind, and let me repeat it for you to be of assistance, which is -- this is a report of August 6th in which it states the following: "Last night Serbian police and military forces shelled Shaptej, Prejlep, and Carrabreg i Poshtem.
