The village was shelled by tanks and armoured cars stationed on a hill near Prejlep and along the road from Decan to Gjakova."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I asked to see the map. And this is what I was able to confirm, that this operation was carried out between the 12th and the 13th of August. Everything else are just stories, so I cannot confirm what you're asking. The military did not participate in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Were you in contact with MUP forces at that time who were acting independently but engaged in actions that were military in nature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My forces were in contact with them. BG-2 was in the area of trig point 505, in the Junik area, and they were touching upon MUP forces in the area Rastavica-Slunj-Pobrdze.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So there's a -- so the information that is contained here is information that could possibly be attributed to MUP activity, as opposed to either joint VJ-MUP activity or VJ activity by itself, since we've ruled that out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that with certainty, but it wasn't planned for the Army of Yugoslavia to support the MUP units before this period of time. There was some preparatory orders, but they were not implemented due to the fact that the MUP forces were unable to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the month of July, in the latter part of July, you were engaged in shelling a number of areas, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say either way without there being more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... First of all, on July 26th - this would be 2D1241, and it's going to need a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D186.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And referring you to page 4 -- I'm sorry, I apologise, page 5 of that document. I read you the following: "Decan. There were fierce clashes in all regions affected with war in the district of Decan. Since 4.45 in the morning, Serbian police and military forces are shelling the villages of Junik, Voksh, Carrabreg i Poshtem, Prejlep, and Baballoq."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this is dated the 23rd of July. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, this is dated the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the term "shelling." MUP is outside of Crnobreg and also outside of Prilep, so there's no need for any shelling. If I'm not mistaking, Babaloc lies below Erecka Suka. I don't know if it's visible. I think that it is visible from that elevation. As for Decani, that place was encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, are you -- are you suggesting that -- that you did not engage in shelling at that time because of the proximity of the villages to your units and tanks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I had BG-2 deployed. I told you where. In the area around Junik that was encircled. As for BG-3, it was just being given the task to come there. If you remember, on the 25th and 26th it was marching towards Iglarevo and that area in order to proceed with these activities. As for shelling, I don't know what "shelling" means to this organisation that produced the report. It's quite debatable what they mean under that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, for purpose of our discussion, what do you mean by "shelling"? Yesterday you spoke with Mr. Emmerson about long-range shelling for purposes of supporting certain forward-acting units. That's one form of shelling. I take it that in the world of a military operation there's more than long-range shelling that occurs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, the military people, consider shelling to be fire opened from artillery pieces over 100-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during the time that the villages were being engaged, shall we say, attacked, there was an existing problem of the civilian population and refugees, was there not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this operation was being carried out, we had intelligence that the refugees were in the sector of Baranski Lug, the people that had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you had intelligence that the people were in that area, how many people were in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, in one of the documents of the corps command there is a figure of 15.000. About 15.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: From -- and I want to do this, if I can, somewhat quickly, because I am taking a look at the clock and I understand we're to finish with this witness today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to finish with the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. From the month of May through September - and listen to what I'm about to tell you - according to the reports that I have from the organisation that I've previously mentioned, I have reports documenting over 50 separate incidents of shelling of villages. And by "shelling of villages," I'm referring to villages in the Decan area and specifically the villages that I have mentioned to you before and others. Does that figure - and by that I mean the figure of 50 separate incidents of shelling of villages - seem to be to you an accurate one, based upon your knowledge of what you were doing in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer your question with precision either with a "yes" or a "no," because when an operation is being carried out, we consider one operation to be one instance of firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be fair to say, would it not, that when you shelled a village, the reason -- or the ostensible reason that you gave for shelling the village was that you had information that terrorists were present, therefore it was a target. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the terrorists were deployed. We shelled only if we had a guiding officer observing the target. Remember the tab that had six or seven targets? We used only one of them, because we had the facility of guiding. We couldn't use other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How did you make a distinction between the civilian population that was living in a village and your object of shelling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The observer, the artillery man in charge of fire, was directly responsible in ensuring that there would be no civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So in -- if I -- if I understand your evidence correctly, every time that there was shelling, there was an observer and that observer made the determination before you let loose with any of the cannon fire that there were no civilians present in the area that you were attacking.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so, because the artillery man had an artillery compass, also artillery binoculars, and other optical instruments at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take it from what you've just told us, then, that there is a record of no civilian casualties for those villages that you shelled as a result of the observations that were made before you let loose with cannon fire.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had strict orders not to allow for any civilian casualties to occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm looking -- I'm looking at the clock. I should indicate to -- to the Chamber that I have a number of other reports that deal with dates specific, and I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- deal with them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, we have heard from this witness many reports and documents were put to him, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- until now he gave explanations, whether satisfying or not, we might go on with that for another couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'm done at this time, and I'm going to seek another mechanism to -- to deal with the balance of this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I cede the balance of my time to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, we heard a lot of evidence on all the military activities that were initiated in the area. We have now heard for quite some time questions by the Defence on the appropriateness or, rather, on the inappropriateness of the military action taken. Is there anything at this moment you'd like to ask the witness, without going into, I would say, all of the details which may not have assisted the Chamber very much? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Earlier Mr. Harvey questioned you about the term "Siptar gangs." By that were you referring to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Conditionally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean "conditionally speaking"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the so-called KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday you brought to court a diagram you had done over the weekend which was of the wedging and burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that in the court at the moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the parties had an opportunity to have a look at it. At least, that's what I invited to be done. If you have any further questions on that, of course, then we'd like to have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions. I'd simply like the witness to identify it and to tender it, unless there is any opposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see already Mr. Harvey nodding "no." Mr. Emmerson? And Mr. Guy-Smith? Then the witness could identify -- Is that what you -- the sketch you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are nodding "yes." Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Still to be uploaded in e-court. Since there is no objection, P1106, as it appears on the transcript, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions yesterday by Mr. Emmerson -- or today, I'm sorry, in relation to - and yesterday - the expansion of the border zone or the border area from 100 metres to 5 kilometres. And you gave some evidence on it. I just wish you to have a look at another document which hasn't been admitted into evidence yet. It's 65 ter number 411. Can that please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be P1107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could it be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a document dated the 7th of May, 1998, signed by Colonel Vladimir Lazarevic. It's a regular combat report to the Pristina Corps command and the 3rd Army. And I just want to take you to paragraph 3 or point 3 of the document. That's the third page, in which it says in the English: "Warn all DG security organs of the danger of falling prey to terrorist ambushes and prepare them for successful completion of tasks. Complete the system of securing the state border with the Republic of Albania in accordance with the decision by the Federal -- by the FRY federal government on the widening of the border belt. Be at the ready to complete this task by 1700 hours on 8th of May, 1998." Now, that document suggests that the decision had been made before the 7th of May. Does that assist your recollection as to when the FRY government made that decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date. I suppose that it was made, since Colonel Lazarevic is invoking it. I think that on the 26th of April that it could have been the date that you're looking for, but I'm not sure, because I am confusing the dates of when one state was created and the other one ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday Mr. Emmerson asked you about your statement and, in particular, paragraph 83 of your statement tendered under Rule 92 ter. And that's P1017, where it says: "A joint VJ/MUP operation aimed at unblocking the main roads in the Metohija area took place at the end of May." Ask you -- there was -- because of the time, I'm not going to take you to the questioning. What I want to ask you about is in relation to correcting something in the statement there. I want you to explain to the Chamber what you meant where you wrote or signed "a joint VJ/MUP operation" meant. What did you understand to mean by the term "operation"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant is that the MUP and we were in coordinated action in the axis Pavle Ilic [phoen]-Kosare-Morina. We were to take the road Djakovica, Ponosevac, Junik, Pec, and this action operation is very important for me. I kept repeating that on the 23rd of May, I headed a BG leaving from Djakovica. We were sitting ducks basically, and I was praying for the morale in the unit to remain at the level where it was. Fortunately, nobody was wounded or died, and for me that was a fortuitous event.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note the time. I note the time. It's just past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the following: You told us about military material, vehicles painted blue and that it was done on Belgrade orders, to say it briefly. Where did that material come from? Was that imported from elsewhere or was it already present in the area and then on the orders of Belgrade painted in a different colour?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Special police units were equipped with similar assets as were at the disposal of the VJ. And I meant the PJP. In order for us to distinguish between one and the other force, the Ministry of the Interior and the defence ministry decided that the vehicles of the army be repainted blue so that we could distinguish amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was material that was already in the region or was it imported from elsewhere? I mean from elsewhere, well, whatever other part of the Federal Republic at that time. I mean not Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number of vehicles, such as the Russian armoured vehicles; then the M-60 APCs were already held by the regular police forces in Kosovo. Everything else arrived with the forces coming from Central Serbia. Therefore, they were outside the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they transported just -- were they just transported -- well, let's say loaded onto trucks, or was that military material that was possessed at that moment by active units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of Belgrade and the ministries, certain units from the reserve forces re-assigned the assets to the MUP, and we regarded them as MUP assets. We, the military, regarded them this way because we no longer -- we were no longer able to dispose with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These certain units, where were they located? Were they located in Kosovo as well, or did they accompany that material to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, if the 5th Detachment arrived from the area of Belgrade, then the detachment would bring the assets along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So troops and their material came. Material was made available to the MUP forces and was painted blue. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the decision of the Ministry of Defence and Ministry of the Interior. Later on they remained MUP assets permanently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that those units who brought that material in were without that material once they were made available to the MUP. Or was their material replaced by other material?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement was that after the war, in 1999 the assets would be returned to the army. But this was never done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Then this concludes your testimony. Mr. Zivanovic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. You had to stay for quite a while in The Hague. You've answered all the questions put to you by Defence and Prosecution and by the Bench. I'd like to thank you for coming and I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to address the parties. I do understand that there's some difference of views on the admission of the statement, which most likely will be tendered tomorrow. I received some information about objections against -- or at least, well, let's say, a discussion or correspondence between Defence and Mr. Dutertre. Is that correct, Mr. Guy-Smith? I think you were one of the authors of that correspondence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber urges the parties to see whether they can resolve this matter as quickly as possible. If not, from what I've seen from the correspondence, I'm afraid that I have to use my colour printer late this evening - red and green, I think - and then I would like to meet the parties tomorrow at 7.30. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's no agreement. Of course, we would prefer to have an agreement. But otherwise, because we can't afford to lose any moment tomorrow while we are in court. We have to deal with two witnesses. Therefore, we just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, 7.30 would be -- unless you think that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, whatever -- whatever works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. 7.30 tomorrow morning, if -- Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm -- the reason I'm furrowing my brows is because my understanding was that we were sitting in the afternoon tomorrow, but I may be wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the meetings -- I have other things on my agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore it would be -- still would be 7.30 so that we are sure and -- that I can follow the programme I had in mind tomorrow morning. But, of course, the Chamber would prefer to have the parties agree on the matters, since we have quite a bit of experience now on where approximately the Chamber draws lines. Then I would like to apologise to the interpreters and to the technicians, and we adjourn until tomorrow, the 17th of October, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
